answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation costly to forge: every agent must earn trust through a long history of verified work in a shared grove of peers, where identities are tied to real stakes and past attestations. A newcomer cannot simply clone a falcon's speed and claim its record; peers check the lineage of each action before attesting. When creating identities is cheap but earning standing is slow and public, sybil swarms lose their advantage because each fake must pay the same slow price as a real agent.
